thread.title: Microsoft: This Might Turn Me Into A Bull - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)

author: D.M. Martins Research
title: Microsoft: This Might Turn Me Into A Bull - Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)
text:
I have resisted Microsoft ( MSFT ) for as long as I remember . Not necessarily skeptical of the company itself or its business prospects, I have always found the stock too pricey to justify a rational investment in it. At a long-term forward PEG of 2.0x (see first graph below), MSFT's valuation is higher than those of peers Apple ( AAPL ), Facebook ( FB ) and Alphabet ( GOOG )( GOOGL ), in some cases by a long stretch.
Credit: Macon Daily
But over the past few months, I have developed an interest for companies that run a robust, primarily SaaS-based business and own an appealing product portfolio that gives them dominance within their industries. Perhaps my top-of-mind example is Adobe ( ADBE ), in digital media and marketing, with salesforce.com ( CRM ) in the CRM arena trailing not too far behind.
MSFT PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts The more I look at Microsoft today, the more I believe that it too belongs in this select group of companies with a compelling, prosperous recurring revenue model. Traditionally a software and device maker, Microsoft has been noticeably reshaped by CEO Satya Nadella and its executive team since they took over, in 2014. In the table below, I break down the company's major segments and try to categorize each of the sub-segments or product types under either of the following two umbrellas: mostly recurring and mostly non-recurring sales.
Source: DM Martins, using data from company's SEC filings
The first, more glaring observation is that most of Microsoft's productivity/processes and intelligent cloud businesses seem to be shifting heavily towards a subscription model. The traditional Office commercial suite, for example, appears to have found in its 365 version a high-growth venture that saw revenues increase an impressive 40% YOY last quarter , in constant-currency terms. Dynamics 365 was up 62% and Azure refuses to cool off, with growth having reached nearly 90% in the most recent quarter.
The second observation is that the "more personal computing" segment appears to be the least aligned with the service and subscription trends currently, with Windows OEM licensing, tablets and Xbox dominating the portfolio. Yet, it is worth noting that Microsoft's computing division is the least relevant of the three in operating profit terms: 30% of total company's in fiscal 3Q18. Also, and maybe most importantly, I see perhaps the best opportunities for Microsoft to further transition this segment to a recurring revenue model, with gaming-related services and DaaS (device-as-a-service) potentially producing the best growth rates within the division in the future.
Implications for the stock As Microsoft's own senior director of cloud partner strategy once wrote , "recurring revenue offers revenue predictability", and "the stock market and venture capitalists place a higher value on predictable recurring revenue as it translates into meaningful valuation". In addition, I have argued that revenue predictability also tends to result in smoother stock price performance, meaning that strong investor returns in this case tend to come attached to relatively less volatility -- i.e. a better risk-return dynamic.
See charts below, in which I compare the trailing five-year annual returns and Sharpe ratios (a measure of risk-adjusted returns) for some of the key subscription-heavy companies (in the case of Visa ( V ), a "quasi-recurring" revenue model that I appreciate ) against those of the S&P 500 ( SPY ).
Source: DM Martins Research, using data from Yahoo Finance
Notice how, perhaps counter-intuitively, MSFT has produced better absolute and relative returns compared to the broad, diversified stock market. And while the performance could be in part explain by economic strength and the raging bull of the past nine years, I would argue that revenue predictability plays an important role, and could even soften the blow of an eventual macro landscape deterioration on the company's future financial results.
For the reasons highlighted above, I inch closer to ditching my skepticism and buying MSFT at current levels, even though the stock's value has already nearly tripled over the past five years.
